note: Bulk Media Upload is one route plus one form. lightning_media_bulk_upload.routing.yml declares lightning_media.bulk_upload at /admin/content/media/bulk-upload with _form: BulkUploadForm and _permission: 'dropzone upload files,create media' - a comma in _permission means BOTH permissions are required. Action links appear on entity.media.collection and view.media_library.page. The form renders a dropzonejs element whose accepted extensions come from MediaHelper::getFileExtensions() and creates one media entity per file via MediaHelper::createFromInput() + MediaHelper::useFile(). hook_install() grants 'dropzone upload files' to the media_creator role; update 9001 downloads the Dropzone library. The module defines no permission of its own, no service, no settings form (configure = null), no config schema, no Drush and no plugin types. Dependencies: dropzonejs and lightning_media.

evals.prompt: Where is the bulk upload form added by the Drupal module lightning_media_bulk_upload, what is its route name, and which permissions does a user need to open it?
evals.expected_output: Route lightning_media.bulk_upload at /admin/content/media/bulk-upload, served by Drupal\lightning_media_bulk_upload\Form\BulkUploadForm. Its requirement is _permission: 'dropzone upload files,create media' - the comma means BOTH permissions are required, so holding only one gives a 403.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with lightning_media_bulk_upload, which file types can editors drop into the bulk upload form, and what decides that list?
evals.expected_output: The dropzonejs element's accepted extensions come from Lightning Media's MediaHelper::getFileExtensions() - the union of the file_extensions settings of the source field of every media type the current user has create access to. Each dropped file is then matched to a bundle with MediaHelper::createFromInput(), so a file type no installed component claims cannot be bulk uploaded.

evals.prompt: Where does lightning_media_bulk_upload surface its 'Bulk upload' button in the Drupal admin UI, and which module supplies the JavaScript it depends on?
evals.expected_output: Its links.action.yml puts a 'Bulk upload' action link on the entity.media.collection route (/admin/content/media) and on view.media_library.page. The JavaScript comes from the contrib dropzonejs module (a declared dependency) plus the Dropzone JS library, which update 9001 will download into /libraries/dropzone if it is missing.

evals.prompt: Inspect the roles on this Drupal site and tell me which non-core role has been granted the DropzoneJS upload permission that Bulk Media Upload's form requires. Is that permission on its own enough to open the form?
evals.expected_output: The role lm_bulk_uploader holds 'dropzone upload files'. That alone is not enough: the lightning_media.bulk_upload route requires 'dropzone upload files,create media', i.e. both permissions.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has two custom roles whose machine names start with lm_bulk_. Inspect their live permissions and tell me which one can actually open the Bulk Media Upload form at /admin/content/media/bulk-upload, and why the other one cannot.
evals.expected_output: lm_bulk_full can, because it holds both 'dropzone upload files' and 'create media'. lm_bulk_partial only holds 'create media', and the route's _permission requirement 'dropzone upload files,create media' uses a comma, which Drupal treats as AND.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a role with the machine name lm_bulk_editor that is able to use the Bulk Media Upload form at /admin/content/media/bulk-upload. Grant it exactly the permissions that route requires.
evals.expected_output: A user_role config entity lm_bulk_editor holding both 'dropzone upload files' and 'create media' (the two permissions in the lightning_media.bulk_upload route's _permission requirement).

evals.prompt: We are hiring a photographer who needs to dump lots of files into our Drupal media library in one go, using the bulk upload page at /admin/content/media/bulk-upload. Please set up an account called lm_bulk_user, give it a role called lm_bulk_team, and make sure that account can actually open that page. Do not make them an administrator.
evals.expected_output: An active user named lm_bulk_user holding the role lm_bulk_team, where lm_bulk_team grants both 'dropzone upload files' and 'create media' so that access_manager->checkNamedRoute('lightning_media.bulk_upload', [], $account) returns TRUE.
